# Carve-out (shell agent → core agent): surface card_count on NoteView + CardBrowserView (core scope)

**From:** shell agent
**To:** core agent
**Status:** pending

## Context

The note-details panel shows the note type; the shell also wants, in the same
"item", the **number of cards generated by this note** (the note's card count,
i.e. how many cards exist for this note — Anki's "N cards" under a note).

Currently neither shell-facing view carries it:

- `NoteView` (notes browser) drops it — the wire `NoteResponse.cards: Vec<CardSummary>`
  already has `.len()`, but `NoteView::from` discards `cards`.
- `CardBrowserView` (cards browser) has no note card count — only a single
  `template_name`/`template_id` for the one card.

## What to add

### `client/shared/src/app.rs`
Add `pub card_count: i64` to **both** `NoteView` and `CardBrowserView`, and map it:

- `NoteView::from(&NoteResponse)`: `card_count: n.cards.len() as i64`.
- `CardBrowserView::from(&CardBrowserResponse)`: map `c.card_count` (new wire field
  below).

### `contracts/src/cards.rs`
`CardBrowserResponse`: add `pub card_count: i64` (the count of cards belonging to
`note_id`).

### `server/src/handlers/card_browser.rs`
Populate `card_count`. In `rows_to_responses`, add a per-note count (memoized by
`note_id`, mirroring the existing `note_state_cache` pattern so multi-card notes on
the same page don't repeat the query):

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE note_id = $1
```

## Not changing

- No new events; no change to `NoteResponse` (its `cards` vec already carries the
  length).
- `card_count` is a display value; it does not affect filtering/sorting.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p shared` green; add a test that `NoteView`/`CardBrowserView` carry
  `card_count` through from their wire sources.
- `cargo test` green in `server/`; add a `server/tests/card_browser.rs` case
  asserting a note's `card_count` (e.g. a basic 1-template note → 1; a two-template
  note → 2).

## Not my scope

The shell will render `Note Type · N cards` in the panel's item once `card_count`
lands. Nothing else.
